Hmm, actually half of this 2-width border will be behind the texture display area (ReferenceRect draws the border with its center being on the rect edge), meaning it could add some visual noise in case the overlapping checkerboard's / the displayed texture's border pixel colors are semi-transparent.

So correct would be to draw only the 1-width border part outside the texture display area, so no overlapping could happen. The question is how exactly to achieve this. AFAICT can't use MarginContainer(s) for 0.5 offsets as they support only integer margins. One way would be to replace this ReferenceRect with a plain Control and manually draw needed rect on its `draw` signal, like `border_drawer.draw_rect(Vector2(-0.5, -0.5), border_drawer.get_size() + Vector2(1, 1), border_color, false, 1.0);`

Alternative could be e.g. adding different border placement mode(s) to ReferenceRect so you could pick to draw the border inside the rect instead of on its edge (then you could just change such mode and set the width to `1`). But this might be overdoing/overcomplicating, not sure.

---

BTW note that the hierarchy could be flatten a little (so all fitting-in would be done directly by the containers, and there would be no need for `draw_behind_parent`), like:

|--------|--------|

Seems simpler to me, but probably fine as is / not a big deal. :upside_down_face:

Yes, this may happen because checkerboard texture is semitransparent. But from what I saw this overlapping doesn't bring much noise.
I'll try to replace `ReferenceRect` with manual drawing, maybe it will look better (or at least comparable).

About tree flattering - good point, will change it.

Also I found out that `TexturePreview` is used for `Camera3DPreview` which doesn't set texture on creation and current implementation will crash editor on `Camera3D` selection 💀

Fixed it locally.

I removed `ReferenceRect` and connected outline drawing to `TextureRect`.
`_update_centering_container_ratio()` renamed to `_update_texture_display_ratio()` - could be reverted.
Also outline width now could be configured via pubic function `set_texture_display_outline_width()`.
Forward declare these two

@kleonc I removed `+1`

That's indeed subjective (briefly they're the same picture :smile:). I tend to prefer less margins so I'd opt for no `+1`, but if it would be left I wouldn't really care I think. :upside_down_face: (but in such case a comment in the code would be welcome to explaing why `+1` are there)

> After `NOTIFICATION_THEME_CHANGED` function `TexturePreview::_draw_outline()` will be also called.

Yeah, this I'm aware of. I was rather considering that `TexturePreview::_draw_outline()` can be called more often, not only on theme change, so always refetching the border color from the theme seems superfluous. But this is a minor issue, should be fine to leave as is (especially given it's already being done like that across the codebase).

Theme changes are always accompanied by `NOTIFICATION_THEME_CHANGED` and every value can be cached. There is still some code that doesn't use cache, because it's more convenient this way, or the code is just old.

I tried to measure how it affects `TexturePreview::_draw_outline()` calls and it takes ~400ns (Ryzen 5 5600 w/ manually reduced clock 2.11GHz), or ~3%, of total function call.
Anyway, as I see, adding caching is preferable, so I'll add it with next push.
Caching added.
Oh, please also add similar check for `_update_metadata_label_text();` down below (which was added by... me :upside_down_face:), seems like it can be created with null `p_texture`.
Sure! Done.

The only call to `set_texture_display_outline_width` looks like this
```
set_texture_display_outline_width(outline_width);
```
so you are calling this method with a property, and then it sets this property again. Looks like the method can be removed?

EDIT:
Looks like you never set `outline_width` anywhere, it always has the default value of 1.
Not needed in a container.
Actually TexturePreview is a Container itself, so all anchor presets can be removed.

@Calinou I tested it on tablet (11', 2560x1600) and phone (6.53', 2340x1080) and it looked fine without taking EDSCALE into account.
If respecting EDSCALE is preferable, could you please tell – am I right that EDSCALE could not be changed at runtime (without editor restart)? Because this "outline" also affects `MarginContainer` margins.
@KoBeWi I added this as public method for future possible uses, but for now it could be removed for sure.
Yeah we don't add things "for future use", unless it's for something specific you plan to do in the future. The method can be easily added when needed.
`EDSCALE` shouldn't change at runtime, the setting for editor scale requires restarting the editor to be taken into account.
